title: Schemeness descends using affine neighbourhoods of finite geometric point sets
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with algebraic closure $\overline{k}$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], locally of finite type, meaning that its etale scheme charts are locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $X$ is locally separated, meaning that its relative diagonal is representable by immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use algebraic-space fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Form the sheaf fibre product $X_{\overline{k}}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}$, computed on test schemes and agreeing with [def-pc-fibre-product] for schemes. Suppose this sheaf is represented by a $\overline{k}$-scheme $Y$. Suppose further that for every $n\geq0$ and every list of $\overline{k}$-morphisms $y_1,\ldots,y_n:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{k}\to Y$, there is an affine open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] through which all the $y_i$ factor. Then $X$ is represented by a $k$-scheme. No group structure or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0B88 (lemma-scheme-over-algebraic-closure-enough-affines), specialized from decent to locally separated by decent-spaces.tex Tag 088J (lemma-locally-separated-decent).

proof.text: The structure map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a map of schemes, hence locally separated. Composition with $X/k$ makes $X$ absolutely locally separated. Thus $X$ is decent. Every etale scheme chart of $X$ is locally of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has only the ideals $0,k$), hence locally Noetherian. Apply the locally-Noetherian decent-space lemma to conclude that $X$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0B88, first paragraph; decent-spaces.tex Tags 088J and 0BB6.

proof.text: Cover $X$ by open subspaces $O$ admitting a surjective etale affine scheme atlas. Each $O$ is quasi-compact, is quasi-separated by quasi-compact-open permanence, and is still locally of finite type over $k$, since a scheme chart of $O$ is a scheme chart of $X$. Fix such an $O$ and an affine atlas $q:U\to O$. Write $O_{\overline k}=Y\times_XO$, an open subscheme of $Y$. We will give scheme neighbourhoods in $O$ for the images of all finite type points of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0B88, quasi-compact-open reduction (small detail omitted), expanded without assuming that the original affine-neighbourhood property restricts automatically.

proof.text: Let $u$ be a finite type point of $U$, and put $L=\kappa(u)$. By definition $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ is of finite type. The affine scheme $U$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over $k$, hence of finite type. Composition gives $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ of finite type, so $L$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Zariski\textquotesingle s lemma makes $L/k$ finite. Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ be the composite and $x$ its point image, which lies in $O$. Decency and the finite-field-map lemma imply that $a$ is representable and finite.

source.place: Tag 0B88, second paragraph; use finite type atlas points in place of closed points of the space.

proof.text: Its base change to $\overline k$ is the finite map $a_{\overline k}:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_k\overline k)\to Y$. The tensor algebra has finite dimension over $\overline k$ (tensor a finite $k$-basis of $L$: the maps $\overline k^d\to L\otimes_k\overline k$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes c_i$, and $l\otimes c\mapsto(\lambda_i(l)c)_i$ for dual coordinate functions $\lambda_i$ are inverse), hence is Artinian and has finite spectrum. For a prime $\mathfrak p$ its quotient is a finite-dimensional domain over $\overline k$, hence a field: multiplication by any nonzero element is an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space, thus is surjective. This field is $\overline k$: each of its elements is algebraic, and a split polynomial over $\overline k$ annihilating it forces it to equal a root in $\overline k$. Thus every point of $Z$ gives a $\overline k$-rational point of $Y$. Point fibre-product calculus shows that the image $F$ of $|Z|$ is exactly the inverse image of $x$ in $|Y|$. The same calculus shows $F\subseteq |O_{\overline k}|$. Choose an affine open $W\subseteq Y$ containing $F$ using the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0B88, displayed tensor-product fibre and affine W; retain only its finite rational support, so no perfection assumption or reducedness of the tensor algebra is needed.

proof.text: Shrink $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ into $O_{\overline k}$ while retaining $F$. Write its closed complement $W\setminus O_{\overline k}=V(J)$. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ representing a member of $F$, $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Prime avoidance yields $f\in J$ outside all these primes. Then $F\subseteq D(f)\subseteq W\cap O_{\overline k}$, and $D(f)$ is affine. If $F$ is empty take the empty affine open. Replace $W$ by this $D(f)$. This also proves precisely the finite-point shrinking needed when restricting the hypothesis to an open subspace.

source.place: Tag 0B88, omitted detail in the quasi-compact reduction; algebra.tex Tag 00DS and schemes.tex Tag 01I3.

proof.text: Index the finite intermediate extensions $k\subseteq K\subseteq\overline k$ by inclusion. This is a small nonempty directed set: any finitely many algebraic elements generate a finite extension, giving common upper bounds; its union is $\overline k$. Put $O_K=O\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$. On an affine scheme test $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to O$, its pullback is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kK)$. Thus the transition maps are affine. The same affine test formula makes $O_K\to O$ affine. Hence every stage is qcqs by affine-morphism permanence. On affine tests, the ring colimit is $A\otimes_k\overline k$; the affine-spectrum limit formula and etale sheaf descent identify the sheaf limit with $O_{\overline k}$. Equivalently this is the base-change-compatible limit asserted by the algebraic-space affine-limit lemma.

source.place: Tag 0B88, last paragraph: the inverse system of finite intermediate field extensions. Its limit and qcqs hypotheses are made explicit.

proof.text: Since the limit $O_{\overline k}$ is a scheme, schematic-stage descent gives a finite intermediate field $K_0$ with $O_{K_0}$ a scheme. Every later $O_K$ is a scheme by the same lemma. Pass to the directed tail $K\supseteq K_0$, whose limit remains $O_{\overline k}$. Its transition morphisms are affine and its stages quasi-separated. Affine-open limit descent applied to the affine $W\subseteq O_{\overline k}$ gives a finite $K\supseteq K_0$ and an affine open $W_K\subseteq O_K$ whose inverse image is exactly $W$.

source.place: Tag 0B88, last paragraph, finite scheme model and affine-open descent; no Galois closure is required.

proof.text: The map $O_{\overline k}\to O_K$ is surjective on points: given any field-valued representative over $K$, the tensor product with $\overline k$ is a nonzero algebra over that field and has a prime, producing a lift after a residue-field extension. Nonzeroness follows by extending $1\in\overline k$ to a $K$-basis. For any point of $O_K$ above $x$, such a lift belongs to $F$, hence to $W$; the equality $W=W_K\times_K\overline k$ therefore puts the original point in $W_K$. Thus $W_K$ contains the entire fibre of $p:O_K\to O$ over $x$.

source.place: Tag 0B88, last paragraph: the descended affine contains the whole fibre; this pointwise argument also applies to inseparable extensions.

proof.text: The projection $p:O_K\to O$ is representable surjective finite locally free. Indeed on a scheme test $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to O$ its source is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kK)$. A $k$-basis of $K$ gives a finite $A$-basis, so the finite-free spectrum lemma gives finite local freeness; these affine tests cover every scheme test. Every point lifts, since its residue-field tensor product with the nonzero finite field extension $K$ is nonzero and has a prime (use a basis containing $1$). Apply the finite-locally-free fibre-neighbourhood criterion to $p$ and the affine $W_K$. It gives an open scheme subspace $N_u\subseteq O$ containing $x$.

source.place: Tag 0B88, final conclusion, with decent-spaces.tex Tag 0BA1 replacing the finite-Galois specialization Tag 0B87.

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq O$ be the union of these open scheme subspaces $N_u$, one for each finite type point $u$ of $U$. Open subsets correspond to open subspaces. On any scheme test $T\to N$, their inverse images are open subschemes covering $T$, so these representable open subfunctors cover $N$. Since $N$ is an fppf sheaf it is a Zariski sheaf; the schemes criterion therefore makes $N$ a scheme. The inverse image $q^{-1}N$ is an open subset of $U$ containing every finite type point, so point detection gives $q^{-1}N=U$. Surjectivity of the atlas and point calculus imply $N=O$. Hence $O$ is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0B88, schematic-locus conclusion; atlas finite-type-point detection replaces sober closed-point detection.

proof.text: The open subspaces $O$ of step 2 cover $X$ and are now represented by schemes. On every scheme test their pullbacks are open subschemes covering that test. The algebraic space $X$ is a Zariski sheaf, and the schemes criterion applied to this representable open cover gives a representing scheme. Its structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the natural transformation corresponding under Yoneda to the given structure map of $X$, so it is a representing $k$-scheme. This includes empty $X$ and needs no global quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 0B88, local-to-global reduction and conclusion; Schemes Tag 01JJ.

Step 4: L⊗k̄ is finite-dimensional and Artinian with residue fields k̄, and no reducedness is used (checked on inseparable L). The image-preimage calculus gives F = fibre of x. Step 5: elementary prime-avoidance shrinking into O_k̄. Steps 6-7: the finite-subextension system is directed with affine transitions and qcqs stages. Its limit is O_k̄, so the schematic-stages lemma applies, and exists_isAffineOpen_preimage_eq gives W_K. Step 8: elementary lifting puts the whole fibre in W_K. Step 9: O_K→O is representable, surjective and finite free on affine tests, so the 0BA1 node gives N_u. Steps 10-11: the schemes criterion together with finite-type-point detection give O and then X. lean.statement: theorem isRepresentable_of_geometric_affine_neighbourhoods (k Ω : Type u) [Field k] [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosure k Ω] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (hlft : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (hlsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω))) (hY : Nonempty (yoneda.obj Y ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))).op ⋙ X.obj.obj)) (haff : ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : Fin n → (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω))) ⟶ Y)), ∃ V : Y.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ z : Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ V.toScheme, z ≫ V.ι = (y i).left) : ∃ Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)), Nonempty (yoneda.obj Z ≅ X.obj.obj)
lean.note: The base change is its functor of points on Over (Spec Ω), obtained by restriction along Over.map (Spec.map (algebraMap k Ω)); a natural isomorphism with yoneda.obj Y expresses representation by the given Ω-scheme. Local finite type is tested on every representable étale scheme chart, and local separatedness on the relative presheaf diagonal. Every finite list of Ω-rational points factors through an affine open, including n = 0. No new notions, stronger separation, group structure or quasi-compactness assumptions.
